items.entity: tip load on the free (right) edge
items.description: Sec. 3.5 only says 'cantilever beam (tip load, fixed left edge)'. Where on the 60-element right edge the load acts is not stated; it would only be visible in the unavailable Fig. 6 density plots. Mid-height and bottom-corner loading are both standard cantilever conventions.
readings: right edge at mid-height (y = 0.5*H)
bottom-right corner (y = 0), a common convention, e.g. the 88-line-code cantilever
top-right corner (y = H); mirror image of the bottom-corner case

items.description: 'Tip load' (Sec. 3.5) suggests a concentrated load, but the text does not say whether it acts on one node or is spread over several nodes or a short edge segment.
readings: point load on a single node
load split equally over 2-3 adjacent tip nodes (about 1-2 element lengths)
uniform traction over a short right-edge segment (e.g. ~5% of H) centred on the tip point

items.description: No load direction is given anywhere (Sec. 3.5). A transverse (vertical) load is the conventional cantilever reading. Flipping the sign of this single linear load leaves compliance and layout unchanged; an axial or inclined load would be a different problem and is not a natural reading of 'tip load'.
readings: vertical, downward (-y)
vertical, upward (+y)

items.description: No load value is given (Sec. 3.5, Table 4). The reported compliances (~76-81 in Table 5) look like normalized units, but this is never stated.
readings: |F| = 1 (normalized)
a physical value, e.g. 1 kN

items.description: Only the ratio E_min/E0 = 1e-9 and nu = 0.3 are given (Sec. 3.1, Sec. 3.5). E0 itself is never stated.
readings: E0 = 1 (normalized)
a physical value, e.g. 210 GPa (steel) or 70 GPa (aluminium)

items.entity: 2-D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: The 2-D benchmarks (Sec. 3.5) do not say whether plane stress or plane strain is used. With nu = 0.3, plane strain acts like plane stress with an effective nu of about 0.43 and a different stiffness, which can slightly change the optimum.
readings: plane stress
plane strain

items.description: No thickness is given for the 2-D cantilever (Sec. 3.5, Table 4). Compliance scales with 1/t.
readings: t = 1 (unit thickness)
another value

items.entity: design domain physical size and element size
items.description: Table 4 gives only the grid '120x60'. Physical length, height and element size are not stated. By convention there are 120 square elements along the beam axis x and 60 through the depth (aspect 2:1), and the r_min values (1.1-4.0) are in element widths. With square plane-stress Q4 elements, a point load and r_min in element units, uniformly scaling the domain changes nothing in the layout.
readings: L x H = 120 x 60 with unit square elements
L x H = 2 x 1 with element size 1/60
L x H = 1 x 0.5 with element size 1/120

items.description: The element formulation is not stated anywhere. Sec. 3.5 'Linear solver' only mentions SciPy direct sparse factorization for the 2-D problems.
readings: 4-node bilinear quadrilateral (Q4), 2x2 Gauss integration (88/99-line standard)
Q4 with reduced/selective integration
8- or 9-node quadratic quadrilateral

items.description: Sec. 3.5 states Vf = 0.40 but not which field it is applied to (design rho, filtered rho-bar or projected rho-tilde from Eqs. 3-4). In three-field SIMP these volumes can differ a lot at beta = 32 (main loop and tail). 'Satisfying the volume constraint' is also used as a validity test for snapshots, with no tolerance given.
readings: mean of physical (projected) density rho-tilde = 0.40
mean of design density rho = 0.40
mean of filtered density rho-bar = 0.40

items.entity: initial design / role of the random seeds
items.description: The starting density field is not given. Results are averaged 'over n = 5 independent random seeds' (Sec. 3.5), and Sec. 1.2 mentions runs 'perturbed by different random seeds'. Yet the fixed and schedule-only controllers show sigma = 0.000 (Table 5), which points to a deterministic uniform start.
readings: uniform rho = 0.40 in all elements
uniform 0.40 plus a small seed-dependent random perturbation

items.description: Sec. 3.1 says only 'OC method with move limit delta'. The damping exponent and the Lagrange-multiplier bisection bounds and tolerance are not given.
readings: standard OC (top88/top99neo): damping exponent 0.5, lambda bisection to ~1e-3 relative tolerance
OC with damping exponent 0.3
standard OC with a much tighter bisection tolerance (e.g. 1e-6)

items.entity: best valid snapshot rho* that seeds the 40-iteration tail
items.description: Sec. 3.5 defines rho* as the lowest-compliance field 'satisfying the volume constraint'. The Table 7 footnote and Sec. 4.5 define validity as p >= 3.0 and G < 0.25, while the grayness-gate threshold is 0.20 (Table 3). The text also does not say how compliances computed at different p/beta are compared when picking the 'best' one. This decides where the tail starts for all four continuation controllers.
readings: valid = volume constraint met; best = lowest raw compliance at the current p, beta
valid = p >= 3.0 and G < 0.25 (plus volume met); best = lowest raw compliance
valid = p >= 3.0 and G < 0.20 (plus volume met)

items.description: Sec. 3.4 says only that 'r_min is tightened in the late stage'. The start value, end value and timing are not given (they appear only in Fig. 9).
readings: r_min = 1.5 until iteration 225, then 1.2 (last 25% of N)
r_min = 1.5 until beta reaches its cap (~iteration 80), then 1.2
linear decrease 1.5 -> 1.2 over iterations 225-300

items.entity: three-field continuation baseline: beta start, first doubling and cap
items.description: Sec. 3.4: 'beta doubles every 10 iterations after the ramp'. The start value, the first doubling iteration and the cap are not given. Doubling without a cap up to iteration 300 is impossible. Only Fig. 9 shows the trajectory (beta >= 16 by iteration 80).
readings: beta = 1 until iteration 30, doubled at 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, capped at 32
same, but capped at 64 (Table 2 upper bound)
first doubling right at iteration 30 (beta = 2), capped at 32

items.entity: three-field continuation baseline: move limit delta
items.description: The move limit for this baseline is never given in the text (Sec. 3.4). It is only plotted in Fig. 9.
readings: delta = 0.2 constant (as in the fixed controller)
delta = 0.2, reduced to 0.05 in the late stage along with r_min

items.description: Sec. 3.4 gives 'step-wise p ramp (+0.75 per 10 iterations)' with no start value or cap.
readings: p from 1.0, +0.75 every 10 iterations, capped at 4.5 (reached ~iteration 50)
p from 1.5: 3.0 at iteration 20, 4.5 at iteration 40
same ramp but capped at 5.0 (Table 2 bound)

items.description: Sec. 3.4 says only 'beta raised only once p >= 3.0'. The increment rule, rate and cap are not given (Fig. 8 shows G crossing 0.20 near iteration 60).
readings: beta doubled every 10 iterations once p >= 3.0, capped at 32
same, capped at 64
beta follows the Table 1 targets (1 -> 4 -> 16 -> 32) once p >= 3.0

items.entity: expert heuristic: r_min and move limit delta
items.description: The text gives no r_min or move-limit values for the expert heuristic (Sec. 3.4). They are only in Fig. 9.
readings: r_min = 1.5 and delta = 0.2 constant
r_min 1.5 -> 1.2 and delta 0.2 -> 0.05 in the late stage

items.entity: schedule-only ablation: stage timing and interpolation
items.description: Sec. 3.4 and Sec. 4.3 say it uses Table 1 with 'the same budget breakpoints' (beta <= 4 until 50% = iteration 150; beta = 32 only from 75% = iteration 225). But Sec. 4.3 also says it 'commits to beta = 32 by iteration 80', and the Fig. 9 caption says beta >= 16 by iteration 80. How p and beta are interpolated inside the Table 1 ranges is not stated either.
readings: Table 1 breakpoints at iterations 24/150/225, linear interpolation inside each stage
Table 1 values applied piecewise-constant per stage (steps at iterations 24/150/225)
compressed timing reaching beta = 32 by ~iteration 80 (e.g. stages advanced after the minimum lengths PHASE.penal = 22 and PHASE.sharp = 16 iterations)

items.entity: LLM agent parameter trajectory (p, beta, r_min, delta, restarts)
items.description: The system prompt is not provided and the preview Gemini model cannot be pinned. Table 6 lists only excerpted calls of one run; the full trajectory is only in Fig. 9. The text also contradicts itself on the gate period (iterations 85-134 in Sec. 4.2, 90-130 in Table 6, G > 0.20 until ~150 in Fig. 8). It is also unspecified which parameters stay active after a snapshot reload.
readings: replay Table 6 values piecewise-constant between listed calls, with restarts at iterations 165, 200, 225 and 300
linearly interpolate between the listed Table 6 calls
re-implement a controller from Table 1 plus the hard gate beta <= 8 while G > 0.20 (trajectory will differ)
deterministic fallback ramp (PENAL_RAMP = 12, BETA_DOUBLE = 10)
